lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hey Carmen, Luis here. How's your Wednesday going?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tell me how the drinks on the weekend went this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I didn't do it. I kept saying tomorrow, tomorrow.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's real progress.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, but you don't know my schedule.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You really shouldn't be drinking at all after cancer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Having a glass of water between drinks is an easy way to slow down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, we had a birthday party, there was so much food.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the drinks on the weekend fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, it was a long weekend with family, you know how it is. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You really shouldn't be drinking at all after cancer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm doing the best I can.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe keep it to 3 drinks on the weekend?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 4. Maybe 5.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Carmen, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Praise is thin given she reported not acting
Knee pain as reason not to walk
Acknowledges her expertise on her schedule
Practical tip, offered without asking permission
Family events and food as reasons to keep drinking
Explores fitting drinks into her day
Asks what is doable next week
Proposes a specific limit of 3 drinks
Plans walking alternative for rainy days
Sets midweek text and two-week follow-up
Closing; did not confirm new time

flags.reason: Repeated directive pushing (lines 10, 12, 15, 17, 25) without asking permission; undermines autonomy.
Absolute 'shouldn't be drinking at all' statement, repeated at line 25 after participant pushback.
Repeated the same directive after participant said 'I'm doing the best I can'; no reflection of her effort.
Ambivalence ('didn't think I'd like it, but I do') not reflected or explored.
Self-proposed 3-drink limit got a generic 'your call' instead of reflection and affirmation.
Participant asked for a later time; coach did not confirm a new time before closing.

score.summary: Carmen proposed a concrete goal (3 drinks on weekends) and identified a rainy-day walking plan, which the coach helped to frame. However, the coach repeatedly used directive and absolute language about drinking and health, and missed chances to reflect her change talk and ambivalence.
strengths: Set a specific goal with a confidence rating (line 30-31) and a backup walking plan (line 33).
Used 'It's completely your call' and 'You know your schedule better than anyone' to support autonomy (lines 9, 14).
Set a clear next contact: midweek text and a two-week follow-up (line 34).
coaching_tips: Replace 'You really shouldn't be drinking at all after cancer' (line 17) with a question asking permission to share health information.
Reflect her change talk at line 28 and 31 (e.g., 'You're thinking 3 drinks is realistic, a 4 or 5') before asking the next question.
Explore the ambivalence in line 24 ('I didn't think I'd like it, but I do') with a complex reflection instead of moving on.
Acknowledge her effort at line 26 ('You're working hard with a lot going on') rather than repeating the directive.
Confirm the new call time requested at line 35 before ending the call.
